summary: DeviceRegistry caches its validated devices keyed by the registry file's stamp (dev, inode, size, mtime, ctime). Every frame-path read (list/lookup/is_current/authorize/controls_any and with_authorized_projects for read operations) stats the file and reuses the cache when the stamp is unchanged, with no flock and no parse; any atomic replace (all zenpi writers) or in-place write changes the stamp, so revocation still takes effect on the next frame. Write operations keep the cross-process lock and a fresh load across their commit.
commands_run: cargo test --locked --all-features --no-fail-fast --test remote_listener --test remote_subscription --test remote_subscription_tls --test remote_auth --test remote_device_grants --test remote_security --test remote_faults --test remote_concurrency --test remote_android_ack_interop --test remote_android_approval_interop --test remote_android_model_interop --test remote_android_session_interop --test remote_android_terminal_interop --test remote_android_workspace_interop --test remote_android_worktree_interop --test remote_android_interop

validation_result.validator_revocation: same test: revoke then next is_current false and authorize refused (1 fresh read); remote_auth in_place_commit_under_the_lock_reloads_current_permissions_instead_of_a_cached_grant; remote_auth/remote_security/remote_device_grants revocation tests pass
validation_result.registry_reads_per_frame_before: flock + open + parse + validate for is_current per emitted frame and again in with_authorized_projects per dispatch (4 per subscription batch)
validation_result.registry_reads_per_frame_after: one lstat; parse only when the stamp changes

notes: Changed semantics (deliberate, per the row): read paths no longer take the registry flock, so a held lock no longer makes reads or authentication Busy; only writes (with_authorized_projects for write operations, register/revoke/set_permissions/self-revoke) stay Busy after the bounded 100 ms wait. A read that races a commit is linearised before it. Four existing tests encoded the old read-Busy behaviour and were updated: remote_auth registry_contention_* (reads lock-free, self-revoke still Busy) and short_lock_release_* (now: prime the cache, in-place commit under the lock, next authentication is Unauthorized); remote_headless_commands registry_busy_* (reads succeed, select/prompt still Busy, no submission); remote_tui_pairing committed_tls_write_* now forces the delivery refusal with a transiently unreadable registry instead of a held lock (outcome still unknown_outcome, exact retry still idempotent; code is unauthorized instead of busy) and production_host_pair_* expects authentication to succeed while the lock is held. A reader that catches a non-atomic in-place writer mid-write fails closed (InvalidRegistry, not cached). On non-unix there is no stamp and nothing is cached. The test-only read counter is a cfg(test) thread_local. No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code; no new unsafe; one new Mutex (the cache) inside DeviceRegistry, which callers already share through Arc.
